headline: The shell builds, opens offline and keeps the capture core well tested, but two of the slice's own done-when tests are red on GitHub's emulator (the other-origin bridge and the unchosen-app check), so neither non-negotiable has passing device evidence. The OTP filter also errs both ways: some live codes are stored, and some real payments are silently dropped.

findings.title: Done-when 3 is red on CI, and its test can't prove the bridge is refused to another origin
findings.detail: `ShellTest.c_a_page_from_another_origin_gets_no_bridge_and_cant_navigate_the_shell` fails on GitHub Actions' emulator at the branch's HEAD (run 37881271168). It asserts `typeof window.Capacitor === 'undefined'` on `http://127.0.0.1:4173`, which serves the same web build. But the web bundle imports `@capacitor/core`, which defines `window.Capacitor` itself on any origin, so that assertion can never pass. The assertion that matters, `typeof window.androidBridge === 'undefined'` on the next line, never runs. So the spec §17 non-negotiable (*the native bridge answers no other origin*) has no passing evidence anywhere. The first half of the test passed: `location.href = other` kept the WebView on our origin.
findings.repro: gh run view 37881271168 --log-failed   (ShellTest.kt:99). In Chromium: open any page of the preview build and evaluate `typeof window.Capacitor` and `typeof window.androidBridge`.

findings.title: Done-when 4's unchosen-app test is red on CI; it races its own marker, so the non-negotiable is unproven on a device
findings.detail: `CaptureListenerTest.a_notification_from_an_unchosen_app_never_reaches_storage` fails on the emulator: the unchosen notification's text is in the outbox (`expected:<0> but was:<1>` at line 59). The test posts as `com.android.shell` while only Ryt is chosen, then calls `settle()`, which immediately adds `com.android.shell` to the chosen list to post a marker. `cmd notification post` returns before the listener's callback runs, and `Capture.post` reads `Chosen.get()` when that callback arrives. So the 'unchosen' notification is very likely judged with the app already chosen. Either the test races, which is the likely case, or a notification from an unchosen app really reached storage, which would be a Blocker. As written, the test can't tell the two apart. The marker needs a different package from the one under test, or the test must wait for the listener before widening the list.

findings.title: The OTP/TAC filter keeps common one-time codes: OTP glued to digits, "code is", Malay "kod anda", "PIN is"
findings.detail: Matching is by whole words, and a phrase may not be followed by a letter **or a digit**. So `OTP123456` doesn't match `otp`. The list also has no phrase for the most common generic forms: `Your … code is 482910`, `Kod anda ialah …` (only `kod tac`/`kod otp`/`kod pengesahan`/… are listed) and `Your PIN is …`. A chosen app (Grab, a bank) posting any of these is stored in the outbox, raw, and B07 would sync it to the server. Android 15+ hiding OTP notifications from listeners is the first line on the owner's phone, but the spec keeps this filter as the second, and friends' phones vary.

findings.title: The OTP filter silently drops real payments that mention TAC, OTP or a security warning, with no record
findings.detail: `otp-keywords.txt` says *a dropped message is ... never a completed payment*, but that isn't so. The bare words `tac` and `otp`, plus `do not share`, `never share`, `jangan kongsi` and `jangan dedahkan`, match payment notifications that carry a security footer, and merchants whose printed names contain the word. Each is dropped before storage and leaves no trace, so it can never reach *Needs attention* (spec §6.2: an unknown format appears there with its raw text kept). The owner would see a missing payment only as an unexplained gap at a balance check. The current samples in docs/notifications.md have no such footer, which is why the suite is green.

findings.title: The branch's "never caches the API" e2e test is decorative: a worker that caches /api/ stays green
findings.detail: `production.spec.ts` › *the worker is served fresh and never caches the API* only checks that `sw.js` contains the string `'/api/'`. Probe: I changed the worker to cache every `/api/` GET, and all five production tests stayed green. The behaviour itself is correct today. QA's FLOW-10 made two online `/api/` calls and found no `/api/` entry in any cache, and offline `fetch('/api/…')` rejected. But once B05's API returns money, nothing in the suite would notice a regression.

findings.title: The heartbeat's "last event" moves on every duplicate and replay, so a dead capture can look alive
findings.detail: Found by reading; not reproduced, since it needs a device. `Capture.store` calls `Heartbeat.event(context)` **before** `outbox.insert(...)`, whatever the insert returns. Every reconnect replays the notifications still showing (`onListenerConnected`), so after a reboot or rebind *Last notification captured* jumps to now, though nothing new arrived. The soak's evidence (done-when 6: *as the heartbeat timestamps show*) and B07's *no bank event for 48 h* watchdog both read this time. `event_at` should move only when `insert` returns true.
findings.repro: Read apps/shell/android/app/src/main/java/io/github/ztsia/sen/capture/Capture.kt, store(): `Heartbeat.event(context)` then `outbox.insert(d.event)`. On a device: post a chosen notification, wait, toggle notification access off and on; Settings → Capture shows a new last-event time.

findings.title: The dedupe key hashes title and expanded text too, beyond spec §6.2, and is frozen once B07 syncs
findings.detail: Spec §6.2 and the brief define the key as hash(package + key + `when` + text). The implementation adds the title and the big text. An app that fills in a notification's expanded text in place, with the same key and `when`, becomes a second event, which would be a second payment once templates read it. The code comment says the definition *must never change once events sync*, so it should be settled now, as a decision or a spec edit. It isn't in D115.
findings.evidence: bigText added, same key/when/text -> different dedupe key: true

findings.title: The dedupe key's separator claim is overstated: U+001F inside a field collides
findings.detail: `DedupeKey` says *no two different events can join to the same string*. A field containing U+001F does collide. It's harmless in practice, but the comment shouldn't promise more than the code does. Length-prefixing or JSON-encoding the fields would make the claim true.
findings.evidence: U+001F inside a field collides: true
